doc.title: Bill Easley interviewed by Monk Rowe, via Zoom, November 1, 2021

chapter: Army, Miles Davis and George Benson
title: Miles Davis in Seattle, then joining George Benson
summary: His inner voice story: in army uniform he heard Miles in Seattle, fled, then was told to get with a giant and joined George Benson in January 1968.

story.theme_name: Drafted: musicians in the military and the war years
story.community_name: Drafted: service bands, USO shows and the war years

blocks.x: Do you feel you had like an internal voice or something that told you it was time to move on?

Oh yeah, man. See the internal voice, oh my God we could talk four hours about that. Again, I know I talk a lot but let me, let me tell you about the internal voice. Back in the army, stationed in Fairbanks, Alaska. Now around this time I’m 20 years old, right? So at one point I’m trying to figure out what am I going to do when I get out of the Army. Because I’d actually been working, I had a nice steady gig before I got drafted. Now I said when I get out I won’t have that youth going for me, and they won’t be talking about this little 19-year-old [gap]. Because I’m going to be 20 years old. I’ll be like an old man, you understand? So I’m trying to figure out now what am I going to do? So I go on leave and I’m going through — I stopped in Seattle, Washington. And Miles was playing there at a club called — oh I can’t think of the name right now. Cannonball made a live record there. I can’t think of the name of the club. But Miles Davis, Herbie Hancock, Ron Carter, Wayne Shorter, Tony Williams, they’re working at this club. I’m on my way going back to Fairbanks and I’ve got my army uniform on. So I get this idea, I says I’m going to go to the club and I’m going to go see Miles Davis. And when they take a break I’m going to go up to Miles and say hello Miles, my name is Bill Easley and I play saxophone and so and so, and Miles is probably going to say oh really? Why don’t you go get your horn and come play with us. And that’s what the voice in my head is telling me that this is how it’s going to be you see. So I walked in the club and I’m dressed in my army greens and when they hit it was like some people had come from outer space, man. I had no idea what I was listening to. And I got — it was like an out of body experience and I got up from my chair and I stood right in front of the band and I watched a whole set and they took me to a journey in outer space that I’d never anticipated. By the end of the set my whole idea of going up to Miles and introducing myself disappeared. The voice in my head said, “Go back to your hotel and hide under the bed.” You understand? Because this is, in other words you may want to re-think what you want to do. Maybe you will become a chiropractor or something because this music thing may not be for you. But the voice said, clear as a bell, “Just go back to your hotel and just get under the bed.” You know. So now I’m trying to get out of the club, I’m trying to leave, and they’re changing audiences and I’m — and my hat, I’d left it under the chair where I was originally sitting. You know? So I’m looking all around and I feel these piercing eyes on me, and at the end of Miles’ outstretched hand is my army hat. And Miles says, “Is this what you’re looking for?” You know. And I grabbed the hat and

I ran out of the club. I just ran out of the club. I didn’t even know, remember my name. I just ran out of the club. And so it was devastating but well, you know, there’s other things in the world that I could do. Then I go back to the base, clear as a bell the voice in my head said, “You’ve got to get with a giant. You’ve got to get with a giant.” In other words that means you’ve got to get with somebody that knows more than you do and so on and so on. So I listened to the voice and I went back to practicing and really getting as serious as I’ve always been at it. And so I came out of the army in November of ’67. By January of ’68 I’m out on the road with George Benson. You understand? For two years. And he was a giant. You understand? I’m talking about when we were playing straight ahead, this was before he became a superstar. This is when we were out playing those joints and being on concerts with Miles and with Duke Ellington and with Monk and you name ‘em. We’re playing at the Vanguard maybe opposite Bill Evans or a week opposite Herbie Hancock and the sextet and so on and so on. So that’s where that evolved from that voice in your head.
